data.title: Share buybacks in Ericsson during the period November 16 - November 20, 2026
data.description:
STOCKHOLM, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- During the period November 16 - November 20, 2026, Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (publ) ("Ericsson") (LEI code 549300W9JLPW15XIFM52) repurchased own Class B shares (ISIN: SE0000108656) as follows:

The share repurchases are a part of the share buyback program of up to SEK 15,000,000,000 which Ericsson announced on April 16, 2026, and which runs between April 23, 2026, and March 31, 2027, at the latest. The Board of Directors intends to propose to the 2027 Annual General Meeting that the repurchased shares, other than those used to fulfil Ericsson's obligations under its share-related incentive programs, are cancelled.

The share buyback program is executed in accordance with the Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council on market abuse (MAR) and the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1052 of 8 March 2016 supplementing MAR (the Safe Harbour Regulation).

All acquisitions have been carried out on Nasdaq Stockholm by Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE on behalf of Ericsson. A full breakdown of the transactions is attached to this announcement.

Following the repurchases above, Ericsson's holding of treasury stock amounts to 132,415,894 Class B shares. There are in total 3,371,351,735 shares in Ericsson, 261,755,983 shares of Class A and 3,109,595,752 shares of Class B.

Prior to transactions carried out during week 47, the Bank held 123,422,799 own shares, corresponding to 7.04% of issued share capital. During this round of repurchase of own shares the Bank has purchased in total 21,033,099 own shares or 1.20% of issued shares, and the total purchase price thereunder is ISK 2,925,682,866.

In this round of share buybacks the aim is to repurchase own shares of the maximum amount of 25 million shares, corresponding to 1.43% of issued share capital, the total purchase price for repurchased shares however not exceeding ISK 3,000,000,000 in total. This round of share buybacks commenced on 2 October 2026 and was to remain in force until 31 December 2026, unless the conditions on the maximum amount of shares or purchase price is met before that time.

The Bank holds 126,849,355 own shares, representing 7.24% of issued shares in the Bank.

The share repurchase programme is carried out in accordance with the applicable law, including the Act on limited liability companies No. 2/1995, Regulation No. 596/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council on market abuse, Commission delegated regulation (EU) 2016/1052 of 8 March 2016, the Act on Measures Against Market Abuse No. 60/2021 and regulation 1290/2025 on the same subject. data.title: Thai appeal court halves jail term of lawmaker convicted of royal insult
data.description:
Thailand's Appeals Court on Monday halved a six-year jail sentence imposed on an opposition lawmaker over a social media post deemed to have insulted the country's powerful monarchy.

Thailand has among the strictest lese majeste laws in the world, with jail terms of up to 15 years for each case of defaming, insulting or threatening the king, queen, heir apparent or regent.

People's Party lawmaker Rukchanok Srinork, a former activist known locally as "Ice", was sentenced by a lower court in 2023 to six years in prison over an X post she made in 2021 and another that she shared, in violation of lese majeste and computer crimes laws.

The court on Monday said it acquitted her of sharing the post and halved the jail term.

Pending her appeal, Rukchanok, who has denied wrongdoing, kept her seat in parliament and was re-elected in February this year.

Rukchanok said she was granted bail following Monday's verdict, while maintaining her innocence and pledging to take the case to the Supreme Court.

"I will perform my duties in a way that befits the dignity of a member of parliament," she said. "I will not let the people down."

At least 199 people in Thailand were sentenced to jail terms for alleged insults of the monarchy between May 2014 and July 2026, according to the legal aid non-profit group, Thai Lawyers for Human Rights.

Under Thailand's constitution, a lawmaker can lose their seat following imprisonment under a final court judgement, subject to certain exceptions.

data.title: Dalian iron ore slides on weakening China demand, falling steel margins
data.description:
Dalian iron ore futures slid on Monday, dragged down by persistently lower demand and shrinking steel margins in top consumer China, while the Singapore benchmark stabilized after touching a four-year low last week.

The most-traded iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange narrowed its daily loss to close daytime trade down 0.3% at 654 yuan ($98.02) a metric ton.

"Ore prices will likely bottom out following a wave of steep falls," said analysts at broker Yongan Futures.

Demand for the key steelmaking ingredient remained weak as thinner margins for steelmakers and lackluster steel demand curbed appetite for restocking of feedstocks.

As of November 19, data from consultancy Mysteel showed average daily hot metal output, a gauge of iron ore demand, had slipped for six consecutive weeks. Output was down 0.3% from the week before to an eight-month low at 2.3 million tons, according to the data.

Meanwhile, only around 10% of Chinese steelmakers were operating at a profit as of November 19, versus 38% in the same period a year before, according to Mysteel data.

By 0710 GMT, the benchmark December iron ore (SZZFZ6) on the Singapore Exchange erased earlier losses to climb by 0.43% to $88.85 a ton. The contract, having stayed well below a key psychological level of $90 for five straight sessions, had hit a nearly four-year low at $86.9 on November 17.

"Prices may stage a recovery following an intense release of bearish sentiment, but upside resistance remained large," analysts at broker China Minmetals Futures said in a note.

Other steelmaking ingredients were mixed with coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! falling 0.46% and coke (DCJcv1) rising 0.31%.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were broadly weaker. Rebar shed 0.23%, hot-rolled coil slipped 0.35% and stainless steel lost 0.62%.

($1 = 6.6722 Chinese yuan)

data.title: Singapore's Cooler October Inflation Suggests Prices Peaked in August — Market Talk
data.description: Singapore's cooler headline and core inflation in October suggest that prices likely peaked in August for this year, OCBC chief economist Selena Ling says in a note. In August, headline CPI rose 2.3% from a year earlier, while core CPI climbed 2.2%. Headline CPI increased 1.9% in October, due to a fall in private transport inflation, she says. Meanwhile, core CPI slowed to 1.5% in October, which is the lowest print since May when it was 1.4%. Still, Ling expects core inflation to accelerate in 1Q before easing more discernibly from mid-2027. Rising global energy or food prices could lift import costs more than expected, she notes. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Eurozone Services PMIs Most Likely to Move Euro — Market Talk
data.description: The euro is likely to react mainly to the services component of eurozone purchasing managers' index surveys Monday, Commerzbank's Michael Pfister says in a note. The eurozone has become less dependent on manufacturing and the euro has also tended to react more clearly to services PMIs in the past, he says. Consensus forecasts expect a slight improvement in the services PMI whereas Commerzbank expects a slight decline. The euro could therefore suffer a sizeable drop, he says. The euro rises 0.3% to $1.1001. The eurozone PMI data are due at 0900 GMT.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)
